The exact S2 predicate over scope=PumpControl, source=[*], target=PumpControl.PumpState returned verdict=false with a counterexample confirming no such owner-local edge exists; the only PumpControl-scoped initial edge (transition:line:26) targets the synthetic InitialState leaf, which has zero outgoing transitions.

arguments.reason: This lens audits root reachability, owner-local initial entry, and reachable event-consumer coverage using the exact FCSTM/inspection-equivalent facts. The closed model shows PumpControl has an owner-local initial edge to InitialState (line 26/5) rather than to PumpState, which contradicts NL3's owner-local first-entry contract. cardinality_bindings.basis: NL2 quote 'Within the PumpControl state, there are three main substates: PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState.'; exact_source_inventory.states PumpControl.PumpState/WaterState/MethaneState parent=PumpControl; inspection_equivalent_facts.states state:PumpControl:line:6.
cardinality_bindings.reason: NL2 directly counts three named substates (PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState) as direct children of the PumpControl composite; this is a direct_child_states cardinality obligation over the owner PumpControl, which resolves exactly to state:PumpControl:line:6 in the closed ModelIR. No concurrent-region or explicit-named-member competing reading changes the primary domain because NL2's plain language counts child substates, not regions, even though the FCSTM happens to realize them as three concurrent regions.

result.reason: This lens audits root reachability, owner-local initial entry, and reachable event-consumer coverage using the exact FCSTM/inspection-equivalent facts. The closed model shows PumpControl has an owner-local initial edge to InitialState (line 26/5) rather than to PumpState, which contradicts NL3's owner-local first-entry contract. This same fact also causes PumpState, WaterState, MethaneState and their entire subtrees to be unreachable from root, which in turn makes every declared event consumer (Activate_Pump, Deactivate_Pump, Start_Monitoring, Stop_Monitoring) unreachable despite being declared, and makes the two transition-endpoint contracts (NL4, NL5) refer to unreachable states. The reachable leaf InitialState has zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING), but per protocol this alone does not establish deadlock_freedom absent an explicit progress obligation, so no V1 candidate is emitted for it. I derive one additional contract for the root-level reachability defect on PumpState (the operating substate that NL1-NL5 require the system to reach and cycle among), and bind event_consumer coverage issues to the sparse declared-vs-reachable comparison for the four events using the S3 trigger route where the transition endpoints are exact, and predicate-null W1 for the coverage-scope claims that lack a distinct NL contract.

issues.reason: NL2 establishes that PumpControl semantically owns three operating substates that must be entered/exercised (as NL3-NL5 corroborate with entry/transition obligations). Cross-view grounding shows the closed model's only default path from PumpControl terminates at a dead-end synthetic placeholder, isolating all three region composites from any reachable default entry. This is a global composite-level reachability gap distinct from the narrower NL3 owner-local-edge-to-PumpState defect, so it is derived as its own contract rather than merged into NL3.
issues.requirement_quote: Within the PumpControl state, there are three main substates: PumpState, WaterState, and MethaneState.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: NL3's own initial_entry contract already flags the PumpControl->PumpState edge defect; one could argue this reachability contract is redundant. However, this contract addresses the distinct global reachability property across all three regions (not just the PumpState local-entry role), and per frontier discipline owner default entry and root/composite reachability are independent properties that must both be preserved.
issues.title: PumpControl's default entry reaches only a dead-end placeholder, never the three required operating regions

issues.expected: PumpControl's owner-local initial pseudostate edge must target PumpState as the first-entered child.
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM defines exactly one PumpControl-scope initial edge, '[*] -> InitialState' (transition:line:26), targeting a synthetic InitialState leaf with zero outgoing transitions; there is no PumpControl-scope initial edge to PumpState. PumpState itself only has its own internal initial edge to RunningState (transition:line:10), which is owned by PumpState, not by PumpControl.
issues.reason: The contract requires PumpControl's own initial edge to enter PumpState as first-entered child; the exact closed-model owner-local edge instead targets InitialState, a compiler/source-declared placeholder distinct from PumpState, and that placeholder has no outgoing transition, closing off any subsequent path to PumpState.
issues.requirement_quote: The system first transitions to the PumpState substate, where the pump is activated or controlled.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue PumpControl -> PumpState is unnecessary because PumpState's own internal '[*] -> RunningState' edge exists; but that internal edge is owned by PumpState scope, not PumpControl scope, and per the owner-scoping rule a nested edge cannot satisfy an outer owner's first-entry obligation.
issues.title: PumpControl owner-local initial edge targets InitialState instead of PumpState

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.states (PumpState, RunningState reachable_from_initial=false), inspection_equivalent_facts.reachability {'[*]': ['llms_emp_feedback_final_0002','PumpControl','InitialState']}, verify_facts non_proved reachability:state:PumpState:line:7 and reachability:state:RunningState:line:8.

issues.reason: This is a root-reachability defect distinct from the owner-local initial-entry mismatch: even a corrected PumpControl->PumpState edge would need to close before PumpState becomes actually reachable from the model root, and the verify_facts non_proved reachability rows independently confirm the global gap.
issues.requirement_quote: The system first transitions to the PumpState substate, where the pump is activated or controlled.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: PumpControl itself is reachable and is the named substate-holder, so one might argue the top-level obligation to 'begin in PumpControl' is satisfied; but NL3 specifically requires transitioning into and operating within PumpState, a distinct, currently unreachable, exact substate.

issues.requirement_quote: The system can also transition to the WaterState substate, indicating that the pump is controlling or monitoring the water flow.

The S2 backend receipt for scope=PumpControl confirms verdict=false for the required PumpControl->PumpState initial edge.
